title: Open, Closed, or Open-Weight? The Secret Labels of AI
summary: Have you ever followed a recipe to bake cookies? If you share the recipe, anyone can make those cookies — or even change it to add chocolate chips! AI models work kind of the same way. When people call an AI “open” or “closed,” they’re not talking about whether it’s friendly. They mean: can you see the recipe? A closed AI, like the one inside ChatGPT, keeps its recipe secret. Only the company that made it knows exactly how it works. An open AI shares its recipe — the source code (the instructions) and the weights (what it learned during training). But here’s the twist: some companies share only part of the recipe. They release the weights but not the training data (the ingredients). That’s called “open-weight.” For example, Meta released a model called LLaMa in 2023. They shared the code and weights, but their license said you can’t use it for business. Some groups say that’s not truly open. Other companies, like DeepSeek and Alibaba, released models with fewer rules, and developers loved them. The idea of open source started way back in the 1980s with computer programmers who believed everyone should have the freedom to run, study, change, and share software. Today, the Open Source Initiative says a fully open AI must include the training data too. But that’s tricky — the datasets are huge! So next time you hear about an AI model, ask: is the recipe fully open, or just partly shared?
why_it_matters: Understanding these labels helps you know if you can tinker with an AI model like you can with a recipe—this could affect what tools you can build in the future.

keywords.explanation: The human-readable instructions that tell a computer program what to do.
The learned settings inside an AI model that help it make decisions, like a brain's connections.
The examples and information used to teach an AI model before it is used.
When a company shares the weights of an AI model but keeps some parts secret, like the training data.
A set of rules that tells you what you are allowed to do with software or an AI model.
Large collections of information, like texts or pictures, used for training AI.

background_read: Open source means sharing the instructions (source code) so anyone can use or change a program freely.
This idea grew in the 1980s and led to free software like the Firefox web browser.
Today, big AI companies like Meta (which owns Facebook and Instagram), DeepSeek, and Alibaba have different ideas about how open their AI models should be.
Article_Structure: WHO: AI companies such as Meta, DeepSeek, and Alibaba, and the Open Source Initiative
WHAT: They release AI models in different ways: fully closed, open-weight, or fully open
WHERE: In the global technology industry, especially in the United States and China
WHY: To control how their AI is used and to balance sharing knowledge with protecting business secrets

perspectives.description: Love open-weight models because they can study how the AI works and make improvements.
Argue that keeping AI closed protects their hard work and helps them earn money to keep developing new technology.
Believe all AI should be fully open so that everyone around the world can benefit equally from it.
